data.objective: Provide reusable workflow business integration, durable lifecycle delivery, dashboard task context, persistent attachments, internal session-confirmed signatures, and a replaceable Mock project context without moving business state into platform modules.

requirements.statement: A server-side business module must be able to start the current valid published workflow version by tenant-scoped stable definition code.
acceptance: Unknown, unpublished, or invalid codes create no instance
A successful instance fixes definition ID and version
The legacy definition-ID start remains compatible
requirements.source: User approved fixed-code workflow startup after latest main inspection
counterexample: The business module queries wf_definition
The browser chooses a definition ID

requirements.statement: Workflow instances must persist consistent business type, key, title, round, project display snapshot, action path, and data digest.
acceptance: Inbox, done, detail, timeline, and lifecycle events expose the same context
Action paths accept only internal routes
requirements.source: User approved business context for dashboard and release detail navigation
counterexample: A dashboard task shows only businessKey
An external URL is stored as actionPath

requirements.statement: Workflow state changes and immutable business lifecycle events must be stored in one transaction.
acceptance: Committed workflow transitions retain an event across process restart
Rolled-back transitions leave no event
requirements.source: User approved durable lifecycle events
counterexample: An in-memory callback is the only record
The event commits before a failed workflow transition

requirements.statement: Lifecycle events must be delivered at least once per stable subscriber with persistence, bounded retry, DEAD visibility, and consumer idempotency.
acceptance: A temporarily failing consumer later succeeds
Duplicate delivery has one business effect
An authorized retry can recover DEAD delivery
requirements.source: User approved idempotent pass, return, and terminate events
counterexample: A consumer outage silently drops approval
Retry generates a new event identity

requirements.statement: Legacy and Flowable workflow paths must emit the same STARTED, RETURNED, APPROVED, REJECTED, and TERMINATED event contract.
acceptance: Contract tests cover both engines
Business consumers do not branch on engine type
requirements.source: Current repository has two workflow execution paths
counterexample: Only Flowable completion creates an event
Payload semantics differ by engine

requirements.statement: The dashboard must show up to five current-user inbox tasks and five recent done tasks with links to full lists.
acceptance: Loading, empty, error, forbidden, and populated states render
Full workflow inbox and done pages remain available
requirements.source: User requested unified task information on the home workbench
counterexample: The dashboard uses hardcoded task cards
The full workflow pages are removed

requirements.statement: Workbench tasks must show business title, type, project display name, current node, actor, time, result, and an authorized internal business-detail route.
acceptance: A task opens the intended business detail
Missing legacy metadata has safe fallback display
requirements.source: User approved enriched dashboard task context
counterexample: The UI constructs a route from an unvalidated external URL
A task is identified only by a numeric instance ID

requirements.statement: Workflow approval nodes must support a backward-compatible signatureRequired setting that blocks decision until explicit confirmation.
acceptance: Existing nodes default to unsigned behavior
A required node rejects an unconfirmed decision
The designer exposes the setting
requirements.source: User approved workflow-configured internal electronic signatures
counterexample: Every old workflow suddenly requires a signature
The requirement exists only in frontend state

requirements.statement: Internal signatures must use the current authenticated identity, bind task, round, action, comment, and business digest, and remain immutable.
acceptance: The server ignores client signer identity and does not accept a client-supplied digest
Approval and signature commit atomically against the stored instance digest
Timeline and detail expose the signature evidence
requirements.source: User selected current-login click confirmation without password re-entry
counterexample: The client can submit another signer ID or replace the signed digest
A signature is editable after approval

requirements.statement: A new ccb-attachment platform module must own persistent attachment metadata, storage identity, state, binding, and audit.
acceptance: Business modules store only attachment IDs
Object keys remain private
The attachment module has an independent Maven boundary
requirements.source: User approved persistent business attachments
counterexample: The release module writes MinIO object keys
Temporary preview records are treated as permanent attachments

requirements.statement: TEMP attachments must be restricted to their uploader while BOUND attachments must use a fail-closed business AttachmentAccessPolicy.
acceptance: Changing an attachment ID cannot bypass tenant or owner checks
A missing or failed policy denies access
Repeated identical binding is idempotent
requirements.source: User approved tenant, project, and business ownership controls while formal project authorization remains deferred
counterexample: Any authenticated user can delete a known attachment ID
Policy failure grants access

requirements.statement: Authorized attachments must support metadata, preview, download, controlled deletion, immutable binding evidence, and retryable orphan cleanup.
acceptance: kkFileView preview is reused when supported
Unsupported files can still download when authorized
Expired unbound files are cleaned idempotently
requirements.source: User approved the complete attachment lifecycle
counterexample: Bound attachments are deleted by the generic browser endpoint
Cleanup deletes an active bound attachment

requirements.statement: The frontend must expose a replaceable ProjectContextProvider and Store with temporary Mock projects and persisted current selection.
acceptance: AppLayout, dashboard, and future business pages consume the Store
Replacing the provider does not change consumer APIs
requirements.source: User stated the project module is in progress and requested a page Mock first
counterexample: Every page embeds its own project array
Project selection disappears on refresh

requirements.statement: Mock project context and Mock project membership must be presentation and local-integration data only, never a production server authorization source.
acceptance: Manipulating browser storage does not grant server data access
Formal project authorization remains an explicit dependency
requirements.source: User deferred project membership and data-scope implementation
counterexample: A client projectRef is trusted as permission
Production is declared project-isolated using only Mock data

requirements.statement: Existing workflow by-ID startup, designer, inbox, done, notification publisher, and temporary file-preview behavior must remain compatible.
acceptance: Existing tests and user flows pass
New fields are nullable for old workflow instances
signatureRequired defaults false
requirements.source: Repository compatibility contract and selected incremental approach
counterexample: The existing workflow API is removed
The notification center is reimplemented

requirements.statement: Business modules must use public workflow and attachment contracts without platform dependencies on concrete business modules or private table access.
acceptance: Platform modules compile without ccb-release
Business integration passes public-contract tests
No business repository writes wf or att tables
requirements.source: Platform AGENTS and user requirement for reusable platform capabilities
counterexample: ccb-workflow imports com.ccb.release
A release service updates wf_instance directly

invariants: Workflow terminal state and emitted terminal event remain consistent
Signer identity comes only from the authenticated server principal
Signature and bound attachment evidence is not physically deleted
Object storage keys are never exposed to business clients
Platform modules never depend on concrete business modules
Mock project data never grants server authorization
constraints: Java 17, Spring Boot 3.4.4, MySQL 8.4, Vue 3 and TypeScript
Append-only Flyway V35 and V36; V1 through V34 remain unchanged
Preserve existing com.ccb packages, APIs, and old workflow behavior
Public platform changes require full governance and regression verification
Desktop workbench and approval acceptance only for this requirement
non_goals: Formal project management and project-member authorization
CA or legally binding digital signature
Password, SMS, biometric, email, or external signature verification
External event bus or cross-system integrations
Release application, baseline, and report business logic
Artifact repository and artifact file upload

assumptions.text: Business modules provide stable business context and normalized SHA-256 digests.
assumptions.basis: Release design already requires immutable workflow rounds.
assumptions.falsifier: A business module cannot produce a stable key or digest.

assumptions.text: Business consumers and attachment policies can be discovered as Spring beans in the modular monolith.
assumptions.basis: Current Boot module composes all Maven modules.
assumptions.falsifier: Deployment separates platform and business modules into different processes.

assumptions.text: The future project module can replace the frontend provider without changing consumer APIs.
assumptions.basis: User stated project management is being implemented separately.
assumptions.falsifier: The project module requires a fundamentally different multi-project interaction model.

tasks.goal: Start the current valid published workflow by stable code and persist trusted business context while retaining legacy startup.
input_facts: Definitions already persist tenant, code, status and current version.

Baseline workflow tests pass.
invariants: Unknown or invalid code creates no instance.
Legacy by-ID startup and old-instance reads remain compatible.
Platform contracts do not depend on business modules.

actionPath is a validated internal absolute route.
non_goals: No release business state machine.

action_bounds: Add nullable V35 context and public integration package.
Modify only workflow services and focused tests needed for by-code startup and projection.
acceptance_checks: Valid code starts and fixes definition ID/version.
Unknown, unpublished and invalid definitions leave zero instance writes.
Legacy workflow tests pass.
evidence_required: Focused and full workflow Maven summaries.
tasks.rollback: Revert T1 application code while retaining nullable V35 structures.
stop_conditions: V35 conflicts with latest main.

Legacy API must break.

tasks.goal: Persist lifecycle events atomically and deliver them at least once with bounded retry, DEAD visibility and idempotent consumers.
input_facts: T1 provides persisted workflow business context.
Both workflow paths mutate state in platform services.
Spring can discover consumer beans without compile-time business dependencies.
invariants: Workflow state and event commit atomically.
Event IDs remain stable across retry.
Consumer failures never roll back completed workflow state.
interface_contracts: WorkflowLifecycleConsumer is public and idempotent.
Both engines emit STARTED, RETURNED, APPROVED, REJECTED and TERMINATED consistently.
non_goals: No external broker or cross-process protocol.
action_bounds: Add one event factory, persistent delivery state, bounded dispatcher and protected monitoring/retry API.
acceptance_checks: Rollback leaves no event; commit leaves one event.
Temporary failures retry and exhausted deliveries become DEAD.
Duplicate and stale delivery tests do not regress business state.
evidence_required: Transaction, parity, retry and permission test summaries.
tasks.rollback: Disable dispatcher and revert T2 code while retaining event evidence.
stop_conditions: A transition cannot share the event transaction.
Consumer discovery creates a reverse dependency.
escalation_conditions: An external message broker becomes mandatory.
Flowable private runtime tables would need direct writes.

tasks.goal: Enforce workflow-configured internal signatures using the current authenticated identity and explicit confirmation.
input_facts: AuthUser is the trusted signer source.
V35 reserves immutable signature storage.
Old nodes must default signatureRequired to false.
invariants: Client cannot choose signer or digest.
Signature and workflow decision commit atomically.
Existing unsigned nodes retain behavior.
interface_contracts: Approval nodes expose signatureRequired with false default.
Decision accepts only signatureConfirmed and server derives all evidence fields.
non_goals: No legal digital signature, password re-entry or external verification.
action_bounds: Extend approval-node model, decision validation, immutable evidence projection and confirmation UI.
acceptance_checks: Required unconfirmed decision is rejected.
Non-assignee, round mismatch and missing digest are rejected.
Confirmed current-user evidence is immutable and visible.
evidence_required: Frontend build and browser decision evidence.
tasks.rollback: Disable new signature configuration and UI while retaining written evidence.
stop_conditions: Current task ownership cannot be established server-side.
Signature cannot share the decision transaction.
escalation_conditions: External or legally binding signing is requested.
Security credential flow must change.

tasks.goal: Create a persistent attachment platform module with opaque IDs, fail-closed authorization and retryable cleanup.
input_facts: Existing MinIO and kkFileView adapters pass baseline tests.
V36 is available.
Business modules can provide AttachmentAccessPolicy beans.
invariants: Object keys never reach business clients.
TEMP is uploader-only and BOUND is policy-controlled.
Bound evidence is not physically deleted.
interface_contracts: AttachmentGateway exposes opaque IDs.
AttachmentAccessPolicy fails closed.
FilePreviewUrlProvider retains host validation.
non_goals: No artifact repository, virus scanning or external file transfer.
action_bounds: Add ccb-attachment, V36, Boot composition, preview adapter and typed frontend API.
acceptance_checks: TEMP owner and cross-tenant tests pass.
Binding is idempotent and conflicting binding fails.
Preview/download/delete/cleanup preserve authorization and retry semantics.
evidence_required: Maven reactor, migration and permission evidence.
tasks.rollback: Disable attachment entry points and module composition while preserving metadata and stored objects.
stop_conditions: V36 conflicts with latest main.
Short-lived links require object-key exposure.
Business compile dependency is required.
escalation_conditions: Production storage configuration must change.
Content inspection or artifact management enters scope.

tasks.goal: Expose enriched current-user workflow tasks on the Dashboard and a replaceable presentation-only Mock project context.
input_facts: Dashboard has no workflow summary.
Workflow pages already provide full inbox and done lists.
Formal project authorization is deferred.
invariants: Dashboard lists at most five items each.
Existing full workflow lists remain.
Mock project state never grants server access.
interface_contracts: ProjectContextProvider is replaceable behind one Store.
Workflow task actionPath is internal and validated.
non_goals: No formal project backend, membership or mobile acceptance.
action_bounds: Add one provider/Store, fixed shell selector and compact Dashboard workbench with full states.
acceptance_checks: Project selection persists and long names do not resize the shell.
Dashboard supports loading, empty, error, forbidden and populated states.
Task detail navigation remains internal.
evidence_required: Desktop light/dark browser screenshots, network and console evidence.
tasks.rollback: Remove workbench and project Store while preserving nullable workflow context.
stop_conditions: Rendering requires formal project authorization.
Safe internal routing cannot be preserved.
escalation_conditions: Auth Store or token shape must change.
Mobile acceptance enters scope.

tasks.goal: Register platform contracts and prove end-to-end convergence without including configuration-management business implementation.
input_facts: Public capability changes require registered ownership and compatibility evidence.
Release business logic is a separate approved requirement.
invariants: All R1-R16 retain evidence.
No platform module depends on a business module.
V1-V34 remain unchanged.
interface_contracts: Workflow and attachment public contracts are documented and registered.
non_goals: No automatic commit, push, PR, merge or release.
No release-management business tables or state machine.
action_bounds: Update governance and contracts, run full regression, scope and browser checks, record evidence.
acceptance_checks: Focused and full Maven tests pass.
Frontend build, governance, Flyway, scope and whitespace checks pass.
Desktop browser acceptance has no blocking console, layout or authorization defect.
tasks.rollback: Revert governance and contracts with their corresponding product behavior; retain migration evidence.
stop_conditions: Any must requirement lacks evidence.
Any full regression or scope gate fails.
Migration numbers conflict.
escalation_conditions: A read-only path must change.
A signature or attachment authorization bypass is observed.
